newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tambang Timah down on Busang news.
newsitem.headline: Tambang Timah down on Busang news.

text.p: Shares of state-controlled tin miner PT Tambang Timah fell 400 rupiah to 4,875 rupiah in active trade after partnership details of the huge Busang gold project in East Kalimantan were announced on Monday.
"There is speculation that Timah might not involved in the Busang gold project," a broker with Singaporean firm said.
Timah's corporate secretary Prasetyo B. Saksono declined to comment on the speculation, saying the firm was still awaiting a government announcement.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Monday the company and its Indonesian partners had formed a joint venture with Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc to develop the property.

It said in a statement faxed to Reuters: "The joint venture will be 45 percent owned by Bre-X, 30 percent by two Indonesian companies and their partners, 10 percent by the Republic of Indonesia and 15 percent by Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold."
"The market is still speculating on the local parties who will hold the 40 percent stake in the project," a broker with leading European bank said.

"Previously, we had a meeting with both shareholders of Askatindo Karya Mineral and Amsya Lyna...that we are interested in getting involved in the project. So if we get it, it should be through them," Saksono told Reuters.
Astakindo Karya Mineral and Amsya Lyna have minority stakes in the Busang property in partnership with Bre-X.
